parsed.basis: Cameroon criminalises consensual same-sex activity and, in practice, gender presentation, with appearance-based arrests carrying six months to five years' imprisonment, plus a separate cybercrime offence for same-sex propositions. Littoral, centred on Douala, the economic capital and main port, is where several best-documented enforcement cases occurred, including the 2021 convictions of two transgender women arrested in a Douala restaurant for wearing women's clothing and sentenced to the five-year maximum. Security forces have also been reported to beat detainees, extort LGBTI people, and detain victims of group attacks over alleged conduct and nonconformity. Douala's main prison is described by accused prisoners as brutal, legal defence is scarce, and an LGBTQ organisation there was raided and closed. No local exception, protective regime, or lighter enforcement distinguishes Littoral from the national picture; urban visibility and port policing increase discovery and police-contact risk.
